خَشِىٌّ Dry; (As, JK, S, K;) like حَشِىٌّ; (As, S;) applied to herbage; (As, S;) or to herbs and trees: (JK:) or dry and rotten. (IAar, TA.) A rájiz says, (S,) namely, Sakhr, (TA,) “سَمُّ ذَرَارِيحَ رِطَابٍ وَخَشِىْ
” [Poison of moist cantharides, and dry]; (S, TA;) meaning وَخَشِىٍّ, suppressing one of the two ىs by poetic license. (IB, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
